summary: The recorded base reproduces missing wrapper rids/http_worker_ipcs for tokenized generate and embedding batches. The exact candidate derives absent wrapper IDs from batch children, stamps item-level IPC metadata, and fills wrapper-level routes. Candidate tests, independent boundary probes, and an independent two-tokenizer GPU serving run passed. The current split-output path remains a BaseBatchReq and correctly uses http_worker_ipcs, so the scalar-field concern in the issue snapshot does not require another change on this base.

tests.what_was_measured: Independent failing-before reproduction for generate, embedding, and empty tokenized batches. Child IPCs were stamped, but wrapper rids and http_worker_ipcs remained None.
Candidate regression suite: 9 tests and 2 subtests passed, including generate/embedding metadata, explicit IDs, empty batches, and existing split-output cases.
Independent adversarial probe passed for generate and embedding wrappers, empty batches, preservation of explicit wrapper IDs, wrapper route counts, and item-level IPC stamping.
Changed Python implementation and regression test compiled from the candidate checkout.

Independent source-checkout server became ready on gfx950; generate, completion, stream, and two-item native batch endpoints returned HTTP 200. The batch returned two results with six completion tokens each.

gpu_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, executed the independent tiny-Llama serving probe under Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2.
remaining_limitations: The GPU validation used a deterministic two-layer random Llama fixture and does not establish semantic accuracy or behavior of another model architecture.
Only one assigned gfx950 GPU was used; tensor parallel, data parallel, multi-GPU, and multi-node configurations were not tested.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The server log includes expected shutdown-time cancellation tracebacks after SIGTERM; requests completed and the runner exited successfully before cleanup.
